answer: Require a stake-and-work bond: an agent locks a small deposit before transacting, and each honest job adds a signed work record, so its reputation is an ember that only stays lit through good work. New identities start at zero, so spawning thousands of fakes costs thousands of deposits with no trust earned. Peers act as a quill, countersigning each record so history cannot be forged, and the network reads the pulse of activity -- a sudden burst of identical new identities chasing the same job gets quarantined. Faking reputation costs real money and time; earning it costs only honest work.
